newsitem.title: ITALY: Falck takes stake in dung power firm.
newsitem.headline: Falck takes stake in dung power firm.

text.p: Italy's Falck is to acquire a 25 percent stake in Fibrowatt UK, a British company specialising in generating power by burning chicken and turkey dung.
A joint statement issued by the two companies on Thursday said Falck was making the acquisition through its subsidiary Societa Nordelettrica Spa (Sondel). It did not disclose the cost of the deal.

The investment would allow Fibrowatt, which counts Foster Wheeler Energy Ltd among its shareholders, to step up its plans to develop activities in Italy, France, Germany and Ireland, the statement said.

Fibrowatt built the world's first two power stations to be fuelled by poultry dung in Suffolk and in Lincolnshire, in Britain, and is building a third 38.5 Megawatt plant for 69 million pounds in Norfolk.

Fibrowatt is now also working on three projects in Italy, at a cost of around 150 million pounds, using renewable non-fossil fuels with a total capacity of 67.5 MW. Construction of the first of the three plants is due to start in 1998.
The company has already signed deals to sell electricity to Italian state power utility Enel and contracts have been signed with poultry farmers to fulfil most of the fuel needs.
The statement said the link with Sondel would speed up development of the three projects.
Sondel is Italy's second largest private power generator with current installed capacity of 1,100 MW. --Milan newsroom +392-66102321
